chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie ibn Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave girl who is sold and for her is a husband, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Her sale is her divorce'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a slave girl when she is sold?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *safaqatun talāquhā* (her sale is her divorce), ruling that when a married slave woman is sold, her marital bond is automatically dissolved due to the change in her ownership status. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of slaves in Shia jurisprudence, where the master's right to transfer ownership supersedes the continuity of the marriage contract, distinguishing it from the rules applicable to free women.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slave girl who is sold and for her is a husband. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Her take-over is her divorce’.
